newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Air union rejects survival plan.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Air union rejects survival plan.

text.p: Canadian Airlines Corp's biggest union said on Friday it rejected the carrier's survival plan that would cut wages by 10 percent for four years.

"This is deplorable. Basically, we are being asked to tell (union members) that once again you have to buy your jobs," an angry Davie Ritchie, vice-president of District Lodge 721 of the International Association of Machinists, told reporters.
"We are not prepared to do that."
The IAM represents represents 5,300 of Canadian's 12,000 unionized workers.

Ritchie said an agreement signed six months ago with the company, which saved the carrier C$34 million a year in labor costs, remained in place and that union leadership was not obligated to return to its members with the latest proposal.
Canadian employees have made wage concessions and agreed to layoffs several times since the airline was restructured in 1992.

"The membership has become the bank of last resort for this management and this airline," he said. The 10 percent wage concession was one of several initiatives outlined by Canadian on Friday in a plan to ensure its survival.

Ritchie, saying he did not believe Canadian's assertion that its survival was dependent on the plan, said union officials offered to present ideas to management for bringing Canadian into the black but were rebuffed.

"I don't think that's saying, 'Man, we want you on side.' It's saying 'We're going to run this airline how we see fit and so long as you're prepared to buy your jobs, you're going to be here,'" he said.
Union officials said privately that Canadian's other unions were more likely to accept the survival strategy.
